summary: Verified the Master Brain SSE 'response ended early' bug fix. Backend regression suite (4 tests) all PASS in 87.6s — including the exact repro (6 mobiles + 'Need Earn Burn summary of above customers'), the follow-up 'continue' turn, negative-balance analytics, and single-customer lookup. Every stream terminated with a real `done` event (never `error`, never a cut connection) and each turn finished well under the 60s ingress cap. UI check on /admin/master-brain confirmed a full formatted answer (aggregate totals table + key observations + recommended actions + suggested-actions execute block) rendered for the 6-mobile earn/burn query with NO 'ended early' banner.
critical_code_review_comments: master_brain_routes.py is 1507 lines — recommend splitting (streaming, tools, prompts, action-log) into submodules for maintainability.
MB_STREAM_WALL_BUDGET (40s) is hardcoded; consider making it configurable via env for future tuning against ingress limits.
seed_data_creation: None. Used the 6 pre-existing preview mobiles.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Master Brain SSE regression tests live at /app/backend/tests/test_master_brain_stream.py — reuse for any Master Brain streaming change. The 6-mobile earn/burn turn took ~30-50s in observed runs; test asserts <75s and terminal done event. If the LLM changes cause turns >55s regularly, tighten MB_STREAM_WALL_BUDGET.
rca of the issue: Original bug: LLM issued serial per-customer tool calls for each of 6 mobiles → 8-15 tool round-trips exceeded the K8s ingress ~60s streaming cap → SSE connection was cut before the terminal `done` event, so the UI's stream reader (which only sets finalized=true on `done`/`error`) fell through to its 'response ended early' fallback. Fix (verified): (1) _run_stream_loop now has a wall-clock budget (MB_STREAM_WALL_BUDGET=40s) checked BETWEEN iterations; once budget spent, it calls _final_synthesis to compose the final answer from the trace and returns it — chat_stream then emits a real `done` event. (2) MASTER_ADDENDUM prompt explicitly instructs the LLM to batch multi-mobile reads into ONE run_aggregation with $in instead of looping per-customer tools. Both are working as expected in this test run.
